# Frozen capability inventory

28319 source-surface rows across 735 audited source files; 11774 declared controls/services have planned fixtures; 16545 support declarations are provenance-only; 2375 baseline test cases indexed. None are native acceptance evidence.

This ledger is deliberately finer than a feature checklist: each enum case, configuration field, command/control, exposed service operation and format route gets its own source anchor, story and fixture. Implementation-support declarations remain separately labeled; the row count is not a user-visible feature count.

Run `python3 scripts/audit-capabilities.py` from any working directory. It re-extracts source anchors and verifies frozen refs, file digests, story membership, fixture identities, baseline tests, provenance and license digests. Regeneration with `--write` updates only this JSON and Markdown ledger and resets fixtures to planned; review mappings before accepting a new baseline.

## Frozen provenance

- Compositor: `11d8d7a50992b24fd9a760a1c13b1c01b70aaf30` at `vendor/Compositor`.
- PhotoCatalog: `f4f8d3f12acc77fe5632720702c52a7cfefb5b58` at `vendor/PhotoCatalog`.

See `DEPENDENCIES.json` and `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`; individual retained license/notice hashes live in JSON.

## Limits and unresolved qualification

- Declaration inventory is intentionally broader than user-visible capability count; implementation-support rows are marked separately.
- The lexical extractor is conservative, not a Swift/Rust/TypeScript compiler. File hashes, declaration-set comparison, explicit enum/format/keyboard checks and full file list prevent silent source changes; they do not prove semantic acceptance.
- Exposed capabilities have planned semantic fixture profiles with individual source parameters; support declarations are provenance-only and are not presented as executable fixtures. Baseline test bodies are indexed as source evidence; this audit does not run them.
- Compositor RAW import and Camera Raw Filter are RGBA8 baseline behavior, not live-RAW acceptance. Every retained pixel tool/kernel requires float/color-contract qualification.
- System RAW recognition is dynamic. Freeze representative real camera fixtures per target macOS version; no enumerated camera support claim follows from UTType.rawImage.
- PSD/PSB readers and conversion reports do not establish layered PSD/PSB export; sc-24675/sc-24676 own required writer and compatibility validation.
- Existing PhotoCatalog image exports render its photo recipe. LensWorks must substitute the full layered live-RAW document render, preserve source identity, and adapt export provenance.
- PhotoCatalog private/transport operations are retained behavior contracts mapped to adapter stories, not a promise to preserve the React/Tauri implementation.
- Conditional Rust test modules embedded in product files are conservatively retained as support rows; baseline_test_cases identifies test evidence separately.
- PhotoCatalog itself has no root license file at this pin; application ownership/licensing needs owner disposition while third-party notices are retained.

10465 rows reference baseline test bodies. These are discovery pointers only: tests have not been executed by this inventory task, and token mention does not establish assertion coverage.

## Concrete fixture profiles

Asset recipes and exact per-capability parameter bindings live in JSON. Profiles are planned specifications; fixture construction/execution is still required by the owning story. Every enum variant and source parameter remains separately bound rather than being waived by the shared recipe.

### catalog-service

Inputs: catalog-two.

Open a new catalog; import source; browse with limit=1, then after=first.sequence; get both IDs; repeat import; reopen; rename original folder offline; request both previews.

- imported=2 initially; unchanged=2 on repeat
- two distinct IDs and increasing sequences; no third page
- CR2 metadata width=48,height=32,orientation=6; preview dimensions=32x48
- same IDs after reopen; previews work offline
- browse limit=1001 and negative after reject without changing catalog

### catalog-adapter

Inputs: catalog-two.

Invoke bound source operation with a live opaque catalog handle; serialize/round-trip its exact public request/result; cancel an active import; release returned buffers and handle; exercise invalid/released handle.

- same typed fields and IDs as retained Rust result
- cancelled work reports actual durable boundary and can resume without duplicate IDs
- no Rust panic crosses Swift; invalid/released handle returns typed error; buffers have one owner
- catalog-two source bytes unchanged

### metadata-organization

Inputs: catalog-two.

Import; set rating=3, pick flag, blue label and hierarchical keyword People/Ada; create collection Portraits; add first ID; search/filter; reopen; undo metadata operation; round-trip XMP unknown-property fixture from retained tests.

- first ID appears once in rating/pick/keyword/collection filters; second ID excluded
- rating 3 and keyword hierarchy survive reopen
- undo restores prior values; expected_revision mismatch rejects stale write
- unknown XMP namespace/property and original packet retained; original photo byte hashes unchanged

### offline-relink

Inputs: catalog-two.

Record both IDs and hashes; rename source folder offline; browse and preview; supply same bytes under a new folder; relink; then supply wrong bytes/ambiguous duplicates.

- offline status visible; both cached previews still decode
- verified relink restores availability with original IDs
- wrong or ambiguous replacement produces review/error instead of silently changing source identity
- catalog/preview paths remain separate from original media

### migration

Inputs: lightroom-frozen.

Run source test builder with folders, keywords, collections, recipe and metadata conflicts; capture and seal approval; migrate into an empty catalog; interrupt at retained publication boundary; resume; mutate approval source and retry.

- all source-backed expected counts and relationship assertions in referenced fixture hold
- unsupported payload retained with compatibility report
- resume produces no duplicate images/versions/relationships
- changed source/approval is rejected; Lightroom/source catalog byte hashes unchanged

### raw-develop

Inputs: hdr2, real-raw, layered3.

Decode full source; set exposure +1 EV and temperature 6500 K; paint an opaque red upper-layer stroke; change exposure to +2 EV; save/reopen; compare preview and full export.

Parameters: `{"real_camera_gate": "must select and qualify real-raw before marking passing"}`.

- working buffer preserves negative/highlight values and straight alpha before display/export conversion
- developed source responds below unchanged editable stroke
- source file SHA-256 identical before/after
- recipe/layers survive reopen; full export evaluates live source rather than browse JPEG

### precision-render

Inputs: hdr2, layered3.

Render the same document in full and bounded tile paths; hide/show upper layers; evaluate alpha in zero and half-alpha samples; convert only at display boundary.

Parameters: `{"tolerance": "must be approved in renderer story; no numerical support claim here"}`.

- source float values remain unclamped upstream
- full/tiled paths agree under approved numerical tolerance; no tile seams
- zero-alpha sample has no visible hidden-RGB fringe
- layer order and masks agree in native display and full-resolution export

### layer-graph

Inputs: layered3.

Duplicate the middle layer; move it into/out of group; rename; reorder; toggle visibility; set opacity=0.5; create clipping/reveal/hide masks; merge selected layers; undo; save/reopen.

- layer UUIDs preserved except intentional duplicate; parent/order/visibility/opacity fields round-trip
- hidden or fully masked adjustment/raster contributes zero
- merge appearance matches pre-merge full composite; undo reconstructs graph
- unmodified source assets retain original hashes

Inputs: edge64, layered3.

Translate selected layer by (4,8); rotate 90 degrees; resize canvas to 80x64 with center anchor; crop to [16,16,48,48]; zoom actual pixels and fit; undo each stage.

- document-space feature coordinates follow declared transform mapping

### selection

Inputs: edge64.

Select rectangle [16,16,48,48]; add [0,0,8,8]; subtract [24,24,40,40]; invert; feather 2 pixels; copy/paste selected pixels; cancel a pending lasso.

- selection membership at (20,20)=true before inversion, (32,32)=false after subtract
- feather adds intermediate edge coverage without changing unselected far pixels
- paste preserves RGBA and makes an undoable layer
- cancel pending selection leaves committed document/selection unchanged

Inputs: edge64, layered3, real-raw.

- heal removes isolated defect while unchanged far pixels remain identical
- retouch replay follows source-coordinate mapping after RAW recipe change
- undo removes stroke and original source hash stays identical

### document-exchange

Inputs: layered3.

Save native package; reopen; import retained PSD and PSB test fixtures with groups/masks/text/adjustments; exercise external-change conflict; export required layered exchange and reopen it.

- native layer UUID graph and editable settings round-trip
- PSD/PSB conversion reports identify unsupported payload without silent loss
- layered export needs a real writer: reader-only success cannot satisfy this observable
- malformed/oversized fixture is rejected without replacing current document

### export

Inputs: hdr2, layered3.

Export complete document as JPEG quality=90 with white matte, PNG16 preserve alpha, TIFF32f linear-sRGB and selectable RGB ICC; fit to 32x32 without upscaling; decode bytes; inject output-write failure.

- full layer/RAW/effect result appears, not only source recipe
- PNG16 reports 16 bits/sample and alpha; TIFF32f reports float samples preserving allowed HDR values
- JPEG has explicit matte and no alpha; embedded profile matches selected RGB profile
- fit dimensions obey aspect ratio; source bytes unchanged; failed publication creates no falsely successful output

### backup

Inputs: catalog-two, layered3.

Back up catalog with linked versions/source revisions/editor assets; restore to second folder while originals offline; interrupt/resume job; corrupt one backed-up asset and retry restore.

- original image IDs, layer graph/history/checkpoints and referenced assets remain available
- rebuildable preview semantics retained
- resuming does not repeat completed output or replace source identity
- corrupt asset checksum rejects incomplete restore; source backup remains unchanged

### native-input

Inputs: layered3.

Focus canvas, text editor and numeric field in turn; invoke this exact source command/chord/control; save custom shortcut; reopen settings; exercise cancel/default buttons; test VoiceOver names and focus route.

- canvas shortcut invokes its specified command once; text entry consumes text keys
- custom chord persists and Restore Defaults removes override
- cancel leaves edited settings/document unchanged; disabled state follows source preconditions
- accessibility name/action and focus order expose the same control

### distribution

Inputs: layered3.

Launch packaged signed native application; open known document via file association; inspect update configuration; exercise disabled/unconfigured feed and approved update path.

- document opens in native editor with readable source refs
- package retains required third-party notices
- unconfigured/unapproved feed performs no download and reports correct state
- approved update signature/version checks reject invalid package

### performance-measurement

Inputs: layered3.

Measure native interaction/preview/export on target device under approved resource ownership and record device/OS/revision; repeat same trace only under story authorization.

- raw timing/memory samples saved with trace inputs and device identity
- limits use sc-24694 approved measured acceptance rather than inherited Compositor numbers
- no concurrent resource campaign launched by inventory audit

### tool-lasso

- undo and save/reopen preserve documented committed/transient state

- undo and save/reopen preserve documented committed/transient state
